bashful

/BASH-fuhl/ - the stress falls on BASH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Bashful means shy, excessively timid.

Rico is too bashful to sing the birthday song with the rest of the waitstaff, so he carries the cake instead.

Worked Example

Asked to take a bow at the curtain call, the puppeteer went bashful: she peeked out from the side of the stage, waved once at knee height, and ducked back before the applause could find her.

Bashful is warmer and more specific than plain 'shy'—it names the fluttery, blushing self-consciousness that shows the moment attention lands. A bashful person isn't afraid of people; being looked at is what undoes them.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sheepish: Sheepish is embarrassment about something you just did — caught mid-blunder, you look sheepish about the act itself. Bashful needs no blunder at all: attention alone undoes a bashful person, who blushes simply at being looked at. Sheepish points at a deed; bashful points at an audience.

timid: Timid people hold back out of fear of what could go wrong — the timid swimmer stays where her feet touch. Bashful people are not weighing risks at all; being looked at is what undoes them, and the feeling is blushing self-consciousness rather than fear.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

bold: steps forward without a second thought

brash: bold to the point of pushiness

Where it sits · how far one shrinks from contact — shy → bashful → withdrawn

shy vs. bashful: Shy is the milder, everyday word next to bashful — shyness is a general hesitancy around people that eases once the room feels familiar, while a bashful person blushes the instant every eye turns their way.

withdrawn vs. bashful: Withdrawn goes further than shy—a withdrawn coworker avoids contact altogether, while a bashful one blushes through it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — bash

Root — bash: to be abashed, taken aback (clipped from abash)

Suffix — -ful

Suffix — -ful: full of, tending to

Put it together

Put it together: Bash (a clipped form of abash, 'to fluster or embarrass') + -ful (full of, tending to) = quick to be flustered. Old French esbaïr, 'to astonish,' gave English abash; someone bashful is easily abashed—thrown into blushes the instant eyes turn their way.

Use the root in a new word: abashed

Use the root in a new word: abashed: Caught reading the toast off his palm, the best man looked abashed for a moment, then grinned and kept going.

Word Choice

warm / informal

Bashful is the gentle, affectionate word for shyness that blushes—use it when the discomfort is sweet rather than painful. Its unit-mate diffident is cooler and more adult: diffident people hold back because they doubt their ability, while bashful people just can't stand being looked at. Taciturn, also in this unit, is different again—saying little by habit, with no embarrassment at all.
